kill_fact: No kill. Every load-bearing bear fact verifies against primary sources, but the downside anchor does not match the record's own arithmetic: valuation_method is declared 'sop' and sop_bear computes $124 per share ($27.7B Industrial + $14.2B Transportation - $6.0B net debt = $35.9B on ~290M diluted shares = $123.9), yet bear_px is stamped 135. Nothing in the record derives 135 under the declared method - it is the midpoint of a second, undeclared earnings-multiple path ($8.95 adjusted EPS at 14-16x = $125-143). Under the record's own stated method the adverse case is $124, i.e. -42.6% from $215.87 rather than -37.5%, which deepens an asymmetry the record already flags as DISCOUNT_TOO_SMALL.
corrections: 1) DOWNSIDE ANCHOR (material, typed): bear_px 135 -> 124, the record's own sop_bear output; the record's segment schedule and the $124 figure are internally consistent and I re-checked the arithmetic, so 135 is the outlier. 2) GM-TRAJECTORY TRUTH - the bear survives fully: gross margin computed from the filed statements is 37.25% (Q1 FY26, 1,739/4,669), 36.78% (Q2 FY26, 1,745/4,744) and 35.56% (Q3 FY26, 1,835/5,160), i.e. 1.7pp of compression in two quarters while revenue grew; the year-over-year comparison (Q3 FY25 1,600/4,534 = 35.29%) is +0.3pp, so any 'expanding margin' framing is true only at the operating line and only year over year. Confirmed, not corrected. 3) BACKLOG TRUTH - orders of $5.7B (+27% YoY), Industrial orders +36%, Transportation +19%, DDN orders +70% year-to-date and book-to-bill of 1.1 in-quarter and year-to-date are verbatim in the 22 July 2026 call, so the demand facts stand; but the 'record backlog' itself carries NO dollar figure on the call or in the 10-Q - it is a management adjective, and orders and book-to-bill are management-reported non-GAAP metrics that no filed statement corroborates. Consequence for the bear: its own named falsification tell, 'a single quarter of book-to-bill below 1.0 in Industrial', is not observable from any disclosure, because TE reports book-to-bill only at company level. The tell needs restating as company book-to-bill below 1.0 or a sequential decline in Industrial orders. 4) SELL-OFF SIZE (minor): 'shares fell 6.9% on 22 July 2026' is overstated - the close-to-close move was -4.18% ($209.01 to $200.28) on 8.79M shares versus roughly 3M normal. The direction of the claim holds (a large down day on a beat-and-raise) and the intraday low that day, $190.27, is the 52-week low the record cites as its entry level - so the named $185-195 entry window has already printed once and was bought back within days. No valuation field moves. 5) CONCENTRATION (minor, cuts against the bear): 'DDN and energy generated essentially all of the growth' overstates it. Energy contributed 'well over $100 million' of the company's roughly $600M of growth (Curtin, 22 July 2026) and DDN roughly $200M; ACL +16%, aerospace/defence +12% and commercial transportation +18% carried the rest. DDN plus energy is roughly two-thirds of Industrial's growth and about half of company growth - real concentration, narrower than claimed. 6) MARGIN LABEL (minor): adjusted operating margin was 21.9%, not 22.0% (Mitts, 22 July 2026). 7) COPPER (minor): COMEX copper settled $6.6435/lb on 4 August 2026, about $14,650 per tonne; the 'roughly $14,000 per tonne LME' reading is directionally correct given the COMEX premium - record-area copper confirmed. 8) Not disqualifying but noted: there is no dilution risk - diluted shares fell to 293M and net debt verifies at exactly $4,393M at 26 June 2026 ($5,632M debt less $1,239M cash), and Astrodyne is cash-funded; the acquisition's 'roughly 16-17x operating cash earnings' rests on a mid-30% cash margin never disclosed for Astrodyne, so that leg is an assumption, though management's failure to quantify synergies is confirmed (operational synergies were mentioned, never sized).

corrections_typed.basis: Record's declared valuation_method is 'sop'; its own sop_bear schedule yields $27.7B (Industrial $2.31B x 12) + $14.2B (Transportation $2.03B x 7) - $6.0B net debt = $35.9B / ~290M diluted shares (293M reported at 26 June 2026, Form 10-Q filed 24 July 2026) = $124. The 135 stamp comes from an undeclared EPS-multiple path and is unsupported by any schedule in the record.

evidence: TE Connectivity Q3 FY2026 earnings call, 22 July 2026 (Curtin, Mitts): record orders of $5.7B, +27% year over year and +7% sequentially; Industrial orders +36%, Transportation +19%; DDN orders up over 70% year-to-date; 'We are running a book-to-bill of 1.1, both in the quarter as well as year to date'; 'record backlog position, and this backlog position is a strong growth indicator as we move into our fiscal 2027' - stated with no dollar amount. Adjusted operating margin 21.9%. Astrodyne TDI: 'more than $250 million in annual sales and had a purchase price of approximately $1.4 billion', closing by end of calendar 2026; synergies described as 'operational' but never quantified. Curtin on optical: 'we are not a major player in scale-out. When you think about scale-out, which is almost all optical today, we have a limited position there.'

TE Connectivity Form 10-Q, quarter ended 26 June 2026 (filed 24 July 2026): revenue $5,160M, gross profit $1,835M (35.56% gross margin); versus quarter ended 27 March 2026, $1,745M on $4,744M (36.78%) and quarter ended 26 December 2025, $1,739M on $4,669M (37.25%) - 1.7pp of two-quarter gross-margin compression on rising revenue, confirming the bear's central margin claim. Total debt $5,632M less cash $1,239M = net debt $4,393M. Diluted weighted-average shares 293M, down from 305M at 27 September 2024.

NYSE price history, 21-24 July 2026: close $209.01 (21 July) to $200.28 (22 July) = -4.18% on 8,792,110 shares, intraday low $190.27 (the 52-week low, set on the print day); 23 July close $198.79. Corrects the record's repeated '-6.9% on 22 July 2026' and shows the $185-195 entry level cited in risk_reward already traded once, intraday, and recovered within three sessions (current price $218.78 on 11 August 2026).

COMEX copper (HG) settlement $6.6435/lb on 4 August 2026, about $14,650 per tonne, and $6.6325/lb on 11 August 2026 - copper is holding at record-area levels, so the bear's pass-through-compression mechanism remains live rather than a spot spike that has since resolved.
